{{Short description|American physicist (born 1932)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Alfred Urquhart MacRae''' (born April 14, 1932) is an American physicist.

MacRae was born in New York City on April 14, 1932.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Contributors |journal=IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits |date=October 1969 |pages=297–299 |doi=10.1109/JSSC.1969.1050022 }}</ref> MacRae is of Scottish descent, and learned how to play the bagpipes, which he did throughout college.<ref name="syr"/> MacRae earned his bachelor's and graduate degrees at [[Syracuse University]], where he studied physics.<ref name="syr"/> Upon completing his doctorate in 1960, MacRae began working for [[Bell Labs]].<ref name="syr">{{cite news |title=Engineering Success: Alfred U. MacRae '54, G'57, G'60 a Pioneer in Integrated Circuits, Satellite Communications |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2018/08/20/engineering-success-alfred-u-macrae-54-g57-g60-a-pioneer-in-integrated-circuits-satellite-communications/ |access-date=26 September 2019 |publisher=Syracuse University |date=20 August 2018}}</ref> He was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1964.<ref>{{cite news |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref> MacRae later led his own company, MacRae Technologies.<ref name="book"/> He was the 1994 recipient of the [[J. J. Ebers Award]], presented by the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]]' [[IEEE Electron Devices Society|Electron Devices Society]] at the [[International Electron Devices Meeting]].<ref name="book">{{cite book |title=Review of NASA's Aerospace Technology Enterprise |date=2003 |publisher=National Academies Press |isbn=9780309182447 |page=109 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OWFt2iHCwlAC&pg=PA109}}</ref> In 2003, MacRae was elected to membership of the [[National Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Alfred U. MacRae |url=https://www.nae.edu/30737/Dr-Alfred-U-MacRae |access-date=26 September 2019 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>
